structured_plan.G: Start from the supplied baseline; no integrated candidate exists yet. After research, integrate measured candidates only, then independently validate and confirm the final program.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline is valid (reported mean 0.0404008269 s across three samples, score 0.5) but its six stencil sweeps are serial and do not use the threads argument. The contiguous x loop also offers a separate SIMD opportunity, while multi-step cache reuse is a distinct, higher-risk approach. No per-size or per-thread baseline breakdown is available, so these are hypotheses to measure, not established bottlenecks. Three complementary objectives are useful; more would likely duplicate these areas. Preserve the interface, full output initialization, boundary behavior, six-step parity, tolerance, arbitrary valid n, and official protocol. Compare only correct candidates under compatible harness conditions; do not assume integration gains are additive, and independently confirm final G.

children.objective: Implement and measure spatial OpenMP parallelism for the six time steps, honoring the threads argument for both one- and four-thread budgets. Partition independent interior rows or slabs, preserve a required barrier between time steps and correct buffer swaps, and keep initialization and all boundary values correct. Support arbitrary valid n; compare correctness and native wall-clock time under the unchanged harness, including any overhead or small-workload regression.
children.subject: Thread-budgeted OpenMP parallelism across independent stencil points

children.objective: Optimize the per-point stencil for contiguous x-direction SIMD, using compiler vectorization and/or suitable x86 intrinsics as appropriate. Reduce indexing and neighbor-access overhead where useful, retain correct handling of row ends and arbitrary n, and preserve the specified tolerance without relying on test-size specialization. Evaluate one- and four-thread timings and correctness using the official protocol.
children.subject: SIMD/vectorization of the row-major stencil kernel

children.objective: Explore spatial cache blocking and, where beneficial, correct multi-time-step temporal blocking to reduce repeated working-set traffic, including vsq reuse. Account for the radius-3 halo at every fused time step, arbitrary dimensions and tails, buffer parity, boundary preservation, full output initialization, and scratch-allocation cost. Measure correctness and native wall-clock time against the baseline; retain the approach only if its full cost improves results.
children.subject: Cache-aware spatial and temporal blocking across stencil steps
